interpretation: The harness qualified, but the direct-observation hypothesis failed for both paths. A depth-agnostic linear observer over transported coordinate probabilities did not recover unseen tables at unseen depths. Because the feature map discards relative phase, the result motivates a phase/coherence-aware observer ablation before adding clocks, explicit depth, or a larger neural observer.

split_confound.description: The original table split used memoryTableIndex(table)%2. Because the base-4 table index parity is determined by entity 3's value parity, training tables contain entity-3 values {0,2} while held-out tables contain entity-3 values {1,3}. The held-out evaluation therefore mixes unseen table combinations with unseen marginal labels for one entity.
split_confound.consequence: UP-7 proves failure of the tested magnitude-only direct observer under that split, but does not isolate the cause. It must not be used alone to conclude that phase loss or depth ambiguity caused the failure.
split_confound.corrective_experiment: UP-8 uses a balanced combinatorial split based on sum(values)%2, verifies every entity/value marginal occurs in both train and held-out sets, and compares magnitude-only versus phase/coherence-aware observers under the same transport/depth workload.

observer_architecture_confound.description: The UP-7 observer concatenated global transported-state probabilities with an entity one-hot selector and applied a single linear softmax head. In a linear model, the selector contributes only entity-specific bias terms; it cannot multiplicatively gate/select different transported-state features for different queried entities.
observer_architecture_confound.consequence: UP-7 also confounds direct-state readability with an underpowered query-conditioning mechanism.
observer_architecture_confound.corrective_experiment: UP-8 uses four entity-conditioned heads with identical architecture/training budget and compares magnitude-only versus phase/coherence-aware features at fixed depth and across unseen depths.
